scenario_en: You need to explain to an interviewer how to use a validation set to stop a model from overfitting further.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证 loss 不再改善时停止训练，避免继续记训练噪声。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Early stopping halts training when validation loss stops improving to avoid memorizing training noise.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许验证表现连续多少轮不改善后再停止的阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Patience is the number of validation checks allowed without improvement before stopping.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练中保存的最佳模型参数快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is a saved snapshot of the best model weights during training.

q: 以下哪些是常见的泛化 / 防过拟合技术？（多选）
why: 前三者都在训练阶段限制或监控模型；把测试集用于调参会让最终评估失去意义。
why_en: The first three techniques constrain or monitor training, while tuning on the test set contaminates the one set meant to measure true generalization.
options: L2/weight decay
Dropout
Early stopping
把测试集直接用于调参
options_en: L2 / weight decay.
Dropout.
Early stopping.
Tuning hyperparameters directly on the test set.
optionExplanations: 对；L2 惩罚大权重，限制模型自由度，是最常用的默认正则化。
对；dropout 训练时随机关闭神经元，迫使模型学冗余稳健表示。
对；验证表现不再改善就停止训练，防止继续记忆训练噪声。
错；这样会让测试集失去评估真实泛化能力的作用，污染最终结果。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — L2 penalizes large weights, constraining the model; it's the most common default regularizer.
Correct — dropout randomly disables neurons during training, forcing redundant robust representations.
Correct — training stops once validation performance stops improving, preventing further memorization.
Incorrect — tuning on the test set contaminates it, so it no longer measures true generalization.
q_en: Which are common generalization or anti-overfitting techniques? Select all that apply.

termDefinitions.meaning: 惩罚大权重，让模型更难依赖单一特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L2, or weight decay, penalizes large weights so the model relies less on any single feature.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时随机关闭神经元，迫使表示更冗余。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dropout randomly disables neurons during training, forcing more redundant representations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证表现不再改善时停止训练，避免继续过拟合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Early stopping halts training when validation performance stops improving to avoid further overfitting.

scenario: 小数据图像分类过拟合严重，你要挑出能真正在训练阶段起作用的手段。
scenario_en: A small-data image classifier is badly overfitting and you must pick the techniques that actually act during training.

q: 模型在 notebook 里表现很好，上线却严重掉线，除了过拟合还该怀疑什么？
why: 现实泛化失败不只看曲线，常见是离线评估没有模拟线上可用信息和未来分布，需要从数据管道和评估设计排查。
why_en: A large offline-to-online gap often means the offline evaluation didn't simulate what's actually available and the future distribution in production.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Offline[Good offline] --> Online[Bad online]
  Online --> Leakage[Check leakage]
  Online --> Skew[Check train serve skew]
  Online --> Drift[Check drift]
  Online --> Split[Check split]
options: 这一定是前端页面某处的 CSS 样式出了问题
数据泄漏、train/serve skew、漂移或验证切分错误
模型的参数设置得太少，才会导致训练集表现意外地异常好起来
线上真实用户的行为完全不会对模型产生任何影响
options_en: It must be a CSS styling bug somewhere on the front-end page.
Data leakage, train/serve skew, drift, or an invalid validation split.
Too few model parameters were set, which is why training performance turned out surprisingly great.
Real online user behavior has absolutely no effect on the model whatsoever.
optionExplanations: 离线线上差距是数据和评估层面的问题，跟前端样式无关。
对；这些都会让离线评估看起来很好，却没有真实反映线上会遇到的情况。
参数太少通常导致欠拟合，训练集表现本身就不会太好，这条不成立。
线上用户行为正是模型要预测和服务的对象，怎么会毫无影响。
optionExplanations_en: The offline-online gap is a data and evaluation problem, unrelated to front-end styling.
Correct — these can all make offline evaluation look good while failing to reflect what production actually sees.
Too few parameters usually causes underfitting, so training performance wouldn't look great in the first place.
Online user behavior is exactly what the model predicts and serves, so it can't be irrelevant.
q_en: If a model works in a notebook but fails online, what else should you suspect besides overfitting?

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练或验证时用到了真实上线时不可用的信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data leakage means training or validation uses information that would not be available at serving time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时的特征生成或数据处理逻辑和线上服务时不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Train/serve skew means feature generation or data processing differs between training and production serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上输入、标签比例或特征到标签关系随时间变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift means production inputs, label rates, or the feature-to-label relationship change over time.

scenario: 离线 AUC 0.92 的风控模型上线后掉到 0.71，训练/验证曲线看起来却很正常。
scenario_en: A risk model scoring 0.92 AUC offline drops to 0.71 in production, yet its train/validation curves look fine.

scenario: 高风险模型遇到明显 drift，且模型置信度低，一旦出错代价很大。
q: 可以加入的补救路径是什么？
why: 人工审核能控制高风险错误，并把当前分布的标签反馈进训练；代价是增加成本和延迟。
why_en: Human-in-the-loop review can handle uncertain, high-risk cases while producing fresh labels that reflect the current distribution.
whenOtherWins: 低风险、高吞吐、错误成本低的场景可以更多依赖自动阈值和监控。
tradeoff: 人工审核保证准确 vs 自动化保证吞吐和速度
options: 系统强制让所有样本都自动全部通过检查
干脆把所有相关的监控功能都直接关掉
引入 human-in-the-loop 审核，产出新鲜标签
只是死死盯着训练 loss 这一个指标，完全不看其他任何信号
options_en: Force the system to auto-approve every single sample without exception.
Just turn off every related monitoring feature outright.
Add human-in-the-loop review to produce fresh labels.
Only stare fixedly at the training-loss metric and ignore every other signal.
optionExplanations: 自动全部通过恰恰放大了高代价错误的风险，方向反了。
关闭监控会让漂移和错误更难被发现，风险更大。
对；人工审核能兜住低置信度的高风险样本，还能产出反映当前分布的新标签。
训练 loss 只反映历史数据，看不出线上置信度低、代价大的实时问题。
optionExplanations_en: Auto-approving everything actually amplifies the risk of costly errors — the wrong direction.
Turning off monitoring makes drift and errors harder to catch, increasing risk.
Correct — human review catches low-confidence, high-risk cases and produces fresh labels reflecting the current distribution.
Training loss only reflects historical data and can't reveal today's low-confidence, high-cost cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让人工审核参与到模型决策或标注流程中的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Human-in-the-loop is a workflow where a person reviews or labels cases alongside the model's predictions.

q_en: What remediation path can you add?
scenario_en: A high-risk model sees clear drift, has low confidence, and mistakes are expensive.

scenario: 广告 CTR 模型的分布在「节假日模式」和「平日模式」之间来回切换，每周重训一次的单模型一到节假日就掉分。
scenario_en: An ad CTR model swings between a holiday pattern and a weekday pattern; the single weekly-retrained model drops accuracy every holiday.
q: 除了继续重训，还能怎么用已有模型？
q_en: Beyond retraining, how else can you use the models you already have?
options: 只保留最近一次训练的模型，把更早时段的模型全部下线
保留多个不同时段训练的模型，按当前数据加权
把所有历史数据不分时段合并成一份重训单个大模型
模型不动，人工每天上调下调预测阈值来跟上分布
options_en: Keep only the latest trained model and retire every earlier-period model.
Keep several models trained on different periods and weight them by current data.
Merge all history into one undated pile and retrain a single big model.
Leave the model alone and hand-tune the threshold up and down every day.
optionExplanations: 只留最新模型时，节假日模式一旦回来就没有任何模型见过它。
对；旧时段模型没被丢掉，当前数据像哪段就让哪段说话。
不分时段合并会把两种模式平均成一个谁都不像的折中模型。
手调阈值只能挪判定线，挪不动模型学到的特征权重。
optionExplanations_en: With only the newest model, nothing in the fleet has ever seen the holiday pattern when it returns.
Correct — old-period models are kept, and whichever period matches today gets the weight.
Merging periods averages the two patterns into a compromise that fits neither.
Hand-tuning a threshold moves the decision line but not the feature weights the model learned.
why: 分布在几个已知模式间来回切换时，多模型加权能同时保住旧模式；代价是每次预测要跑多份模型，服务成本随模型数上升。
why_en: When the distribution oscillates between a few known regimes, keeping period-specific models and weighting them preserves the old regime — at the cost of running several models per prediction.
tradeoff: 多模型覆盖多种分布 vs 单模型的服务成本与运维简单
whenOtherWins: 如果旧模式一去不返（单向演进的 concept drift），只留最新模型定期重训更便宜也更准。

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示中被点击的比例，广告排序的主预测目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR, or click-through rate, is the fraction of impressions that get clicked, and it is the main prediction target in ad ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征与标签之间的真实关系随时间改变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concept drift is when the real relationship between features and labels itself changes over time.

scenario: 流失模型已经加了 L2，训练 AUC 0.93、验证 AUC 0.71。有人主张把强度 lambda 调大 10 倍，也有人担心连有用信号一起被压掉。
scenario_en: A churn model already uses L2: train AUC 0.93, validation AUC 0.71. One camp wants lambda 10x larger; another fears it will crush the useful signal too.
q: 正则化强度 lambda 应该怎么定？
q_en: How should you pick the regularization strength lambda?
options: 在验证集上扫一组 lambda，取验证指标最优的那个
选训练集 loss 最低的 lambda，训练拟合最好即最优
沿用框架默认值，认为它与数据量和特征数无关
取能把权重范数压到最小的那个最大 lambda
options_en: Sweep a range of lambdas and keep the one with the best validation metric.
Pick the lambda with the lowest training loss — best training fit means best model.
Keep the framework default, assuming it is independent of data size and feature count.
Take the largest lambda, the one that shrinks the weight norm the most.
optionExplanations: 对；只有没参与训练的那部分数据能看出这条 U 形曲线的底在哪。
训练 loss 对 lambda 是单调的：越小拟合越好，按它选永远选到 0。
默认值没见过你的样本数与特征数，正则强度本就该随两者调。
权重范数最小的极端是全零模型，那已经彻底欠拟合了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — only held-out data can show where the bottom of that U-shaped curve is.
Training loss is monotone in lambda: smaller always fits better, so this always picks zero.
A default never saw your sample count or feature count, and strength should scale with both.
The smallest possible weight norm is an all-zero model, which underfits completely.
why: lambda 太大把有用信号一起压掉变成欠拟合、太小压不住噪声，这条 U 形曲线只有验证集能看到；代价是要多跑几轮训练扫参。
why_en: Too much regularization underfits, too little overfits, and only a held-out validation set reveals the bottom of that curve — you pay for it with extra training runs.
tradeoff: 偏差（正则太强）vs 方差（正则太弱）
whenOtherWins: 样本极少、单次 hold-out 噪声太大时，用 k 折交叉验证扫参更可靠，代价是训练次数翻 k 倍。

termDefinitions.meaning: 正则化项在损失里的权重系数，也常写作 alpha。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lambda is the coefficient that scales the regularization penalty inside the loss, also written alpha.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积：衡量模型排序能力的指标，0.5 相当于随机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC, area under the ROC curve, measures ranking quality, where 0.5 is random guessing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从训练中留出、模型没见过的那部分数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hold-out set is data withheld from training that the model never sees.

scenario: 商品分类模型在头部类目训练误差与验证误差都低，在长尾小类目上两者都高。有人下结论「整体过拟合，加正则」。
scenario_en: A product classifier has low train and validation error on head categories but high train AND validation error on long-tail ones. Someone concludes "it overfits, add regularization".
q: 这个整体结论错在哪？
q_en: What is wrong with that blanket conclusion?
options: 同一模型可能对头部过拟合、同时对长尾欠拟合，要分片诊断
验证误差只要在某处偏高就一定是纯过拟合，加正则总没错
训练误差在头部很低，说明模型已经学到了全部结构
长尾误差高只可能来自标签噪声，与模型容量完全无关
options_en: The same model can overfit the head while underfitting the tail — diagnose per slice.
Any elevated validation error means pure overfitting, so more regularization is always safe.
Low training error on the head proves the model already learned all the structure.
High tail error can only come from label noise and has nothing to do with capacity.
optionExplanations: 对；长尾上两条误差都高是欠拟合信号，全局加正则只会更糟。
把连续的欠表现区间压成一个二元标签，是这类误判的根源。
头部样本多、模式简单，学好头部不代表学到了长尾的结构。
容量或特征不足同样会让稀疏类目学不动，不能只归给标签。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — both errors being high on the tail signals underfitting, and global regularization makes it worse.
Collapsing a continuous band of underperformance into a binary label is exactly the mistake.
The head has many samples and simple patterns; fitting it says nothing about the tail.
Too little capacity or too few features can also stall rare categories, so labels are not the only suspect.
why: 过拟合与欠拟合是一段连续的欠表现区间而非全局二元标签；要按数据切片各自读 train/val 才知道该加容量还是加正则，代价是评估要多维护切片。
why_en: Overfitting and underfitting are two ends of a spectrum, not a global binary label, so you have to read train-versus-validation error per data slice before choosing capacity or regularization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 样本量很小、种类很多的那批类别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long-tail categories are the many classes that each have very few training examples.

scenario: 同一份超参，只换一个随机的 90% 训练子集重训，模型的重要特征排序每次都不一样，验证分数在 ±8 个点之间摆动。
scenario_en: With identical hyperparameters, retraining on a different random 90% subset each time reshuffles the top features and swings validation score by ±8 points.
q: 这个现象说明模型处在什么状态？
q_en: What state does this behaviour indicate?
options: 高方差：模型在拟合噪声与个例，而非稳定结构
高偏差：模型对数据做了过强而错误的假设，学不动
数据漂移：线上分布已经偏离了训练时的分布
数据泄漏：验证集里混进了只有训练时才有的特征
options_en: High variance — the model is fitting noise and outliers rather than stable structure.
High bias — the model makes strong, wrong assumptions and cannot learn.
Data drift — the production distribution has moved away from the training one.
Data leakage — the validation set contains features only available at training time.
optionExplanations: 对；换一批样本就换出一套模式，正是高方差的定义。
高偏差的表现是两条误差都高且稳定，不会来回大幅摆动。
这里根本没上线，换的只是训练子集，谈不上生产分布变化。
泄漏会让验证分数虚高且稳定，不会随子集抽样上下乱跳。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a different sample yields a different learned pattern, which is exactly high variance.
High bias shows up as both errors being high and stable, not as wild swings.
Nothing is deployed here; only the training subset changed, so production distribution is irrelevant.
Leakage inflates validation scores steadily; it does not make them jump with resampling.
why: 训练数据的小扰动导致学到的模式剧烈变化 = 高方差，也就是过拟合的那一端；补数据、降容量或加正则能压住，代价是训练集上的分数会变差。
why_en: When small changes in the training data produce wildly different learned patterns, that is high variance — the overfitting end — and fixing it costs you training-set performance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型对训练样本抽样过度敏感，换一批数据就学出另一套模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: High variance means the model is so sensitive to which training samples it saw that a different sample yields a different learned pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测时拿不到的信息混进了训练或验证特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data leakage is when information unavailable at prediction time sneaks into the training or validation features.

scenario: 线性模型预测传感器读数，训练和验证 loss 都停在很高的位置并早早持平；训练轮数已从 20 加到 200，两条曲线纹丝不动。
scenario_en: A linear model predicting sensor readings plateaus early with both training and validation loss high; the team already went from 20 epochs to 200 and neither curve moved.
q: 下一步最该动的是哪一项？
q_en: What should you change next?
options: 换更高容量的模型或加特征，解除过强的假设
继续把训练轮数从 200 加到 2000，给它更多时间收敛
加大 L2 强度，让权重更小、曲线更平滑一些
扩大验证集比例，重新评估这两条 loss 曲线
options_en: Move to a higher-capacity model or add features to relax the too-strong assumption.
Push epochs from 200 to 2000 to give it more time to converge.
Increase L2 strength so weights get smaller and the curves smoother.
Enlarge the validation split and re-measure the two loss curves.
optionExplanations: 对；假设空间太小时，唯一的出路是把空间本身放大。
曲线已经持平，轮数不是瓶颈，再跑十倍只是烧算力。
更强正则会进一步限制假设空间，把欠拟合推得更深。
换个切分只改评估精度，不会让欠拟合的模型学到新东西。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — when the hypothesis space is too small, the only way out is to enlarge the space itself.
The curves already plateaued, so epochs are not the bottleneck and 10x more just burns compute.
Stronger regularization shrinks the hypothesis space further and deepens the underfitting.
Changing the split only sharpens measurement; it teaches an underfitting model nothing new.
why: 两条 loss 都高且早早持平 = 高偏差，模型假设太强所以学不动，这是选错模型而非训练不够；换更高容量的代价是需要更多数据、也重新打开了过拟合的门。
why_en: Both losses high and flat means high bias — the model is too simple, not undertrained — and buying capacity means you now need more data and reopen the overfitting risk.
tradeoff: 容量（拟合能力）vs 数据量需求与过拟合风险
whenOtherWins: 如果训练 loss 还在降、只有验证 loss 开始回升，那是过拟合，这时才该加正则或早停。

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型对数据做了过强而错误的假设，连训练集都学不好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: High bias means the model makes strong, wrong assumptions and cannot even fit the training data well.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在损失里加上权重平方和的惩罚，压制过大的权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to the squared weights, keeping any single weight from growing large.

termDefinitions.meaning: 验证指标连续 N 轮不再改善就停止训练，取最好那一轮的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Early stopping halts training once validation stops improving for N epochs and keeps the best epoch.

scenario: 情感分类只有 5000 条标注。有人想照搬图像那套增强，对句子做同义替换和随机删词来扩样本，标签一律沿用原句。
scenario_en: A sentiment classifier has only 5,000 labels. Someone wants to copy the CV playbook: synonym-swap and randomly delete words, reusing the original sentence label.
q: 把这套增强搬到文本上，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of porting that augmentation to text?
options: 改写可能连标签语义一起改掉，产出错标样本
文本增强只会让训练变慢，不会影响样本标签的正确性
改写后的句子一定与原句同分布，可以直接当新样本用
文本领域完全没有可用的增强手段，只能花钱重新标注
options_en: Rewriting can change the label semantics too, producing mislabeled examples.
Text augmentation only slows training down; it never affects label correctness.
Rewritten sentences are guaranteed to match the original distribution, so just reuse them.
Text has no usable augmentation at all, so you must pay to relabel from scratch.
optionExplanations: 对；删掉一个「不」或换一个近义词，中性句可能就变成正向句。
把标签污染说成纯性能问题，恰恰漏掉了这里唯一真正的危险。
同义替换只在词面上接近，情感强度与语气分布都可能被改写。
错别字、大小写、无关实体替换这类不改标签的扰动仍然可用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — dropping one negation or swapping a near-synonym can flip a neutral sentence to positive.
Calling label corruption a mere speed issue misses the only real danger here.
Synonym swaps only look close on the surface; sentiment intensity and tone can shift.
Label-preserving perturbations like typos, casing, or unrelated entity swaps still work fine.
why: 图像的旋转裁剪不改类别，而文本改写会连语义一起动，增强出来的是噪声标签；文本增强要先界定哪些扰动确定不改标签，这一步比在 CV 里贵得多。
why_en: Rotating an image never changes its class, but rewriting a sentence can change its meaning, so text augmentation first requires proving which perturbations preserve the label.
tradeoff: 样本量增加 vs 标签保真度下降
whenOtherWins: 当扰动确实与标签无关（错别字、大小写、无关实体替换）时，文本增强同样便宜有效。

termDefinitions.meaning: 计算机视觉：处理图像与视频的机器学习领域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CV, computer vision, is the machine-learning field that works on images and video.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自然语言处理：处理文本与语言的机器学习领域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NLP, natural language processing, is the machine-learning field that works on text and language.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过变换已有样本生成合成训练样本的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data augmentation generates synthetic training examples by transforming the ones you already have.

scenario: 手上有 10 亿条本公司专有格式的无标注日志，但没有任何公开预训练模型见过这种日志，标注只有 2000 条。
scenario_en: You have a billion unlabeled logs in a proprietary format, only 2,000 labels, and no public pretrained model has ever seen this format.
q: 自监督和迁移学习的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between self-supervised learning and transfer learning?
options: 自监督从零自造预训练任务，迁移学习复用现成权重
两者都要先拿到一个公开预训练模型当起点，区别只在微调层数
自监督仍需人工标注，只是标注量比监督学习少一些
迁移学习只适用于图像，自监督只适用于文本领域
options_en: Self-supervision invents its own pretraining task from scratch; transfer learning reuses existing weights.
Both must start from a public pretrained model; they only differ in how many layers you fine-tune.
Self-supervision still needs human labels, just fewer than supervised learning.
Transfer learning only works for images and self-supervision only for text.
optionExplanations: 对；本题没有见过这种日志的现成权重，只剩自造监督信号这条路。
把自监督的起点说成别人的权重，正好抹掉了它唯一的适用前提。
掩码词预测、重建被破坏的输入这类信号全部来自数据本身。
两种方法都跨领域通用，BERT 是迁移学习在文本上的经典例子。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — no existing weights have seen this log format, so inventing a supervision signal is the only path.
Claiming self-supervision starts from borrowed weights erases the very condition it exists for.
Signals like masked-token prediction or reconstructing a corrupted input come purely from the data itself.
Both techniques work across domains; BERT is the classic transfer-learning example in text.
why: 没有覆盖这种日志格式的现成权重时，只能用无标注数据自造监督信号从零学表示；代价是预训练本身要付出大量算力和工程时间。
why_en: When no existing weights have seen your data format, you have to build a supervision signal out of the unlabeled data itself — and pay for a pretraining run.
tradeoff: 自建预训练贴合本域但算力昂贵 vs 复用权重便宜但受原域限制
whenOtherWins: 一旦有覆盖本领域的公开预训练模型，迁移学习加冻结底层比自己从零预训练便宜几个数量级。

termDefinitions.meaning: 从无标注数据自造预测任务（如预测被遮住的词）来学表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Self-supervised learning invents a prediction task from unlabeled data, such as predicting masked words, to learn representations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把在大数据集上预训练好的模型拿来在小数据集上微调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transfer learning takes a model pretrained on a large dataset and fine-tunes it on your smaller one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个用掩码语言建模预训练的文本模型，常被微调到下游任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BERT is a text model pretrained with masked-language modeling that is commonly fine-tuned for downstream tasks.

scenario: 一个上线时训练与验证 gap 很小、线上指标也达标的风控模型，半年后指标持续下滑；复查训练曲线依然健康，代码也没改过。
scenario_en: A risk model shipped with a small train-validation gap and healthy production metrics now degrades six months later, yet its training curves still look fine and no code changed.
q: 这更像哪种失效，下一步查什么？
q_en: Which failure is this, and what do you check next?
options: 数据漂移：先比对当前与训练时的特征分布
过拟合：模型一直在记忆训练噪声，应先加大正则再重训
欠拟合：模型容量太低，应该换一个更大的模型试试
线上 bug：只可能是某个特征的计算逻辑写错导致的
options_en: Data drift — start by comparing current feature distributions against training-time ones.
Overfitting — it has been memorizing training noise, so raise regularization and retrain.
Underfitting — capacity is too low, so try a bigger model.
A production bug — it can only be a miscomputed feature.
optionExplanations: 对；曲线健康说明训练那一刻没问题，变的是之后的世界。
过拟合会在部署当天就露馅，而这个模型上线时表现是达标的。
欠拟合会让训练误差一开始就高，与「上线时达标」直接矛盾。
特征逻辑没改却持续下滑，更像输入分布本身在慢慢移动。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — healthy curves say training was fine; what changed is the world afterwards.
Overfitting shows up on day one of deployment, but this model met its targets at launch.
Underfitting would have kept training error high from the start, contradicting a healthy launch.
Nothing changed in feature code, yet it decays steadily — that looks like the input distribution moving.
why: 泛化良好只保证部署那一刻的分布，之后世界变化照样让同一套模式失效；所以该去监控特征与预测分布，而不是回头重看训练曲线，代价是要长期维护一套监控。
why_en: Good generalization only guarantees the distribution at deploy time; the world can still move afterwards, so you monitor feature and prediction distributions instead of rereading training curves.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产数据的分布随时间偏离训练数据的分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data drift is when the distribution of production data moves away from the training distribution over time.

scenario: 欺诈模型上线时欺诈占交易的 1%，判定阈值定在 0.5。一年后真实欺诈率涨到 3%，特征与欺诈的关系没变，但人工复核队列被淹没。
scenario_en: A fraud model launched when fraud was 1% of transactions with a 0.5 threshold. A year later fraud is 3%, the feature-label relationship is unchanged, and the review queue is flooded.
q: prior probability shift 的直接后果是什么？
q_en: What is the direct consequence of prior probability shift?
options: 原有决策阈值不再校准，命中量和精确率一起偏移
输入特征的分布发生了变化，需要重新做特征工程
特征和标签之间的关系已经改变，必须更换模型架构
模型权重会随时间自动衰减，需要重新初始化再训练
options_en: The old decision threshold is no longer calibrated, shifting both volume flagged and precision.
Input feature distributions changed, so feature engineering must be redone.
The feature-label relationship changed, so the architecture must be replaced.
Weights decay on their own over time, so you must reinitialize and retrain.
optionExplanations: 对；基率从 1% 涨到 3%，同一个 0.5 分数对应的后验风险已经不同。
那是 covariate shift，本题明确说变的是标签比例而非输入分布。
那是 concept drift，本题明确说特征与欺诈的关系没有改变。
权重不会自己变；分数分布的移动来自数据里正负比例的变化。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with the base rate up from 1% to 3%, the same 0.5 score now implies a different posterior risk.
That is covariate shift; here the label proportion changed, not the input distribution.
That is concept drift; the problem states the feature-fraud relationship is unchanged.
Weights do not change by themselves — the score distribution moved because the class balance did.
why: prior probability shift 只改了正负样本比例，模型排序能力仍在，但按旧基率定的阈值会大量误报；先按当前基率重校准阈值比重训更快，代价是要有新鲜标签来估这个基率。
why_en: Prior probability shift changes only the class balance, so ranking still works but the old threshold over-flags; recalibrating is faster than retraining, provided fresh labels let you estimate the current base rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签漂移：目标变量的分布（正负样本比例）随时间改变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prior probability shift, also called label drift, is when the distribution of the target variable changes over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入特征分布改变，但特征与标签的关系不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Covariate shift is when input feature distributions change while the feature-label relationship stays the same.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征与标签之间的真实关系本身发生改变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concept drift is when the real relationship between features and labels itself changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型输出的分数能对应上真实发生概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration means the scores a model outputs actually correspond to real-world probabilities.

scenario: 团队每周自动重训一次模型，但线上真实标签要 30 天才回流，短期内看不到任何准确率数字。
scenario_en: A team retrains weekly, but true production labels only arrive after 30 days, so no accuracy number is available in the short term.
q: 怎么用重训节奏本身当漂移信号？
q_en: How can the retraining cadence itself serve as a drift signal?
options: 每次重训都在同一个固定测试集上评估，看分数是否走低
只比较各次重训自己的训练 loss，越低就说明模型越好
每次重训都换一个新的随机测试集，保证评估足够新鲜
等 30 天真实标签回流后再判断，在那之前不做任何评估
options_en: Score every retrain on one fixed test set and watch whether the number trends down.
Just compare each retrain's own training loss — lower means a better model.
Draw a fresh random test set for every retrain so the evaluation stays current.
Wait the 30 days for real labels and evaluate nothing until then.
optionExplanations: 对；测试集固定住，分数的变化就只可能来自模型与数据本身。
训练 loss 只反映模型在自己那批数据上的拟合，跨批不可比。
每次换测试集等于同时动了尺子和被测物，分不清谁在变。
干等 30 天意味着漂移已经造成一整月线上损失才被发现。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — freeze the test set and any score change can only come from the model and the data.
Training loss only reflects fit on its own batch and is not comparable across batches.
Swapping the test set each time moves the ruler and the object at once, so nothing is attributable.
Waiting 30 days means drift is only discovered after a full month of production damage.
why: 固定 hold-out 测试集把评估的尺子锁死，分数持续下滑就是分布在变的信号；这是标签延迟时最早能拿到的证据，代价是这份测试集本身也会随时间过时。
why_en: A frozen hold-out test set locks the measuring stick, so a steadily falling score points at the data, not the metric — but that test set itself goes stale over time.
tradeoff: 固定测试集的可比性 vs 测试集自身的新鲜度
whenOtherWins: 如果真实标签当天就能回流，直接监控线上精确率/召回率比固定测试集更贴近真实损失。

termDefinitions.meaning: 从训练中永久留出、只用于评估的一份固定数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hold-out test set is data permanently withheld from training and used only for evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实结果标签从线上采集回训练数据所需的延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label lag is the delay before ground-truth labels come back from production into your training data.

scenario: 推荐模型有 2000 维特征，逐维设分布告警跑了一年几乎全是噪声告警，值班每周被误报淹没，真漂移一次也没提前抓到。
scenario_en: A recommender has 2,000 features; a year of per-feature distribution alerts produced almost only noise, drowning on-call in false pages and catching no real drift early.
q: 除了继续调检测阈值，还能怎么做？
q_en: Beyond tuning detection thresholds further, what else can you do?
options: 不追求精确检测，直接把重训提到固定的高频周期
把全部分布告警的阈值统一放宽到几乎不再触发任何告警
只保留上线时的一次性检测，之后不再监控任何分布
停止定期重训，等线上准确率明显掉下来再一次性处理
options_en: Stop chasing precise detection and just move to a fixed high-frequency retrain schedule.
Loosen every distribution alert threshold until essentially nothing ever fires again.
Keep only a one-off check at launch and monitor no distributions afterwards.
Stop scheduled retraining and react in one batch once accuracy visibly drops.
optionExplanations: 对；用固定节奏重训把漂移直接消化掉，绕开了先测准这个难题。
放宽到不报警等于取消监控，却仍背着一整套告警的运维成本。
一次性检测看不到缓慢累积的分布移动，而漂移正是慢慢来的。
等指标掉下来才动，损失已经发生，标签回流还要再等一段时间。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a fixed retrain cadence absorbs drift without first solving the hard detection problem.
Loosening until nothing fires is cancelling monitoring while still paying to operate it.
A one-off check cannot see slow cumulative shift, and drift is usually slow.
Reacting after metrics drop means the loss already happened, plus label lag delays it further.
why: 漂移检测本身很难做准，与其在 2000 维上磨阈值，不如靠高频重训消化漂移；代价是很多次重训其实是白跑的算力，以及更频繁上线带来的流水线风险。
why_en: Drift detection is genuinely hard, so many teams skip it and retrain aggressively instead — paying in wasted compute and in the release risk of shipping models more often.
tradeoff: 精确检测（省算力）vs 高频重训（省诊断成本）
whenOtherWins: 如果一次重训要几天、成本极高，那就值得投入做精准检测，只在确认有漂移时才重训。

termDefinitions.meaning: 当特征或预测的统计量超出设定范围时触发的告警。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distribution alert fires when a feature or prediction statistic moves outside a configured range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真实结果标签从线上采集回训练数据所需的延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label lag is the delay before ground-truth labels come back from production into your training data.

scenario: 团队保留 4 个不同时段训练的模型做加权集成来抗漂移，上线后每次请求要跑 4 份推理，GPU 成本和 p99 延迟都接近翻了 4 倍。
scenario_en: A team keeps four period-specific models in a weighted ensemble to hedge drift; every request now runs four inferences, and GPU cost and p99 latency both nearly quadrupled.
q: 这种集成的代价和常见配套是什么？
q_en: What does this ensemble cost, and what usually accompanies it?
options: 成本随模型数上升，通常配 bandit 或锦标赛挑模型
集成不增加线上成本，多个模型可以先合并成一份权重再部署
集成会自动消除漂移，因此不必再重训其中任何一个成员
只要集成里的模型数量够多，就不必再关心单个模型的时效性
options_en: Cost scales with model count, so a bandit or tournament usually picks which model serves.
Ensembles add no serving cost because the models can be merged into one weight set first.
Ensembles cancel drift automatically, so none of the members ever needs retraining.
With enough members, the freshness of any individual model stops mattering.
optionExplanations: 对；让路由层每次只选一个模型出手，就把成本压回单模型量级。
不同时段训练的模型学的是不同分布，平均权重会毁掉各自的特点。
成员模型全都在老化，集成只是延缓下滑，不是免重训的许可证。
如果所有成员都陈旧，加权平均出来的还是一个陈旧的预测。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a routing layer that picks one model per request pushes cost back to single-model levels.
Models trained on different periods encode different distributions; averaging weights destroys both.
Every member ages too; an ensemble slows the decline, it is not a licence to skip retraining.
If all members are stale, their weighted average is still a stale prediction.
why: 集成把多种分布都留在服务里，但每次预测都要跑 N 份模型，成本和尾延迟随 N 线性上升；实践上常用 multi-armed bandit 或锦标赛只让一个模型出手，用探索代价换回服务成本。
why_en: An ensemble keeps several distributions alive in production but multiplies cost and tail latency by N, so teams usually put a multi-armed bandit or tournament in front so only one model actually serves.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线选择策略：边试探各候选、边把更多流量给表现好的那个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multi-armed bandit is an online policy that explores candidate options while shifting more traffic to whichever performs best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求都快于这个耗时，衡量尾部体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 latency is the time under which 99% of requests complete, a measure of tail experience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图形处理器：深度模型训练与推理的主要算力硬件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GPU, or graphics processing unit, is the hardware that carries most deep-model training and inference compute.

scenario: 两个模型离线 AUC 完全相同：A 把绝大部分权重压在三个强相关特征上，B 加了较强 L2、权重分散在几十个特征。该领域预计未来一年缓慢漂移。
scenario_en: Two models have identical offline AUC: A concentrates weight on three strongly correlated features; B uses heavier L2 and spreads weight over dozens. The domain is expected to drift slowly for a year.
q: 该上哪一个，理由是什么？
q_en: Which one do you ship, and why?
options: 选权重分散的 B，学到的模式更稳健，漂移时退化更平缓
选靠三个强特征吃分的 A，离线同分说明两者泛化能力相同
两者没有区别，离线 AUC 相同就代表未来表现也会相同
选 A，并靠把重训频率提到每天来抵消掉所有分布变化
options_en: Ship B with spread-out weights: sturdier patterns degrade more gently under drift.
Ship A, which leans on three strong features — equal offline AUC means equal generalization.
There is no difference; identical offline AUC implies identical future performance.
Ship A and retrain daily to cancel out every distribution change.
optionExplanations: 对；权重摊开后，任何单个特征分布变化只能拿走一小部分信号。
离线分数只测同分布下的表现，测不出对分布变化的抵抗力。
相同的 AUC 可以由完全不同的权重结构产生，抗漂移能力不同。
重训能追上漂移，但两次重训之间那段窗口仍会断崖式掉分。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with weight spread out, any single feature shifting can only take away a small share of the signal.
Offline scores only measure in-distribution performance, not resistance to distribution change.
Identical AUC can come from very different weight structures with very different robustness.
Retraining chases drift, but the window between retrains still sees a sharp drop.
why: 记住脆弱相关性的模型，一旦那几个特征分布变了就断崖式掉分；正则化逼模型学更稳健的模式，用训练集上的分数换来漂移时更平缓的退化曲线。
why_en: A model that memorized brittle correlations falls off a cliff when those few features move, whereas regularization trades training-set score for a gentler degradation curve under drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时约束模型，使其更难记住噪声，从而提升泛化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regularization constrains a model during training so it is harder to memorize noise, improving generalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积：衡量模型排序能力的指标，0.5 相当于随机。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC, area under the ROC curve, measures ranking quality, where 0.5 is random guessing.

scenario: 你手写 dropout：训练时以 p=0.5 随机关掉神经元，推理时全部打开且不做任何处理，结果推理输出的量级约是训练时的两倍。
scenario_en: You hand-rolled dropout: at training time neurons are dropped with p=0.5; at inference all are on with no adjustment, and the outputs come out about twice as large.
q: inverted dropout 怎么处理这个缩放？
q_en: How does inverted dropout handle that scaling?
options: 训练时把存活神经元放大 1/(1-p)，推理时不做缩放
训练时不做缩放，推理时把所有神经元的输出乘以 (1-p)
训练和推理都按 1/(1-p) 放大，保持两个阶段完全一致
推理时也随机丢弃神经元，让两个阶段的分布保持相同
options_en: Scale surviving neurons up by 1/(1-p) during training, and do nothing at inference.
Do not scale during training, and multiply every neuron output by (1-p) at inference.
Scale by 1/(1-p) in both training and inference so the two stages match exactly.
Randomly drop neurons at inference too, so both stages see the same distribution.
optionExplanations: 对；训练时就把期望补齐，推理路径上一次乘法都不用加。
这是经典（非 inverted）写法，正确但把开销压在每次线上推理上。
两边都放大只是把量级整体抬高一次，训练与推理仍然对不齐。
推理随机丢弃会让同一输入每次给出不同结果，线上不可接受。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the expectation is fixed during training, so inference needs no extra multiply at all.
That is the classic non-inverted form: correct, but it puts the cost on every online inference.
Scaling both sides just raises the overall magnitude; the two stages still do not line up.
Dropping at inference makes the same input return different answers, which is unacceptable in production.
why: 训练时只有 (1-p) 比例的神经元在发数，把它们放大 1/(1-p) 就让激活的期望与全网一致；代价是训练期数值方差更大，换来推理路径干净、零额外乘法。
why_en: Only a (1-p) fraction of neurons fire during training, so scaling survivors by 1 over 1-p keeps the expected activation the same as the full network, leaving inference untouched.
codeSample:
mask = (np.random.rand(*h.shape) > p) / (1.0 - p)  # 训练: 丢弃 + 放大存活项
h_train = h * mask
h_infer = h  # 推理: 神经元全开, 不做任何缩放

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时以概率 p 随机关闭神经元，迫使网络学习冗余表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dropout randomly switches off neurons with probability p during training, forcing the network to learn redundant representations.

termDefinitions.meaning: dropout 的标准实现：把缩放放在训练侧，推理时无需调整。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inverted dropout is the standard implementation that puts the scaling on the training side so inference needs no adjustment.
